editorial.headline: Conventional Guarantees: Financial Commitments, Clearly Defined
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers conventional guarantees for financial obligations, open nationally to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Conventional guarantee activity is about standing behind a financial obligation: a guarantor assures the beneficiary that the guaranteed party’s obligation will be met. Its scope reaches credit and financing extended by financial institutions, loans channelled by savings-and-loan cooperatives to their members, and credit or loan partnership programmes distributed by state-owned enterprises. The work is therefore not merely a promise in the abstract; it concerns identifiable financial commitments and the arrangements through which they are supported.

The remit is deliberately broad within that conventional-guarantee frame. It includes guarantees over debt instruments, instalment purchases, trade transactions, procurement of goods or services through surety bonds, bank guarantees through counter-guarantees, domestic documentary credits, letters of credit, customs bonds and excise guarantees. It also includes management-consulting services connected with guarantee operations, alongside other guarantee activities. The common thread is the provision of a conventional guarantee for the fulfilment of a financial obligation.

The activity is open at every recorded business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That matters because the record does not confine the classification to a single size of operator. A business registering this activity should be able to describe its actual guarantee function with care—whether the underlying obligation concerns credit, financing, a cooperative loan, a trade transaction or a procurement commitment—while remaining inside the conventional-guarantee scope set out here.

Nationally, the activity is marked TERBUKA for PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. Bali does not overturn that position through its permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium for low and medium-low risk activities. The Bali record places large-scale OSS risk at Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi and states that the activity is not blocked by that moratorium. In practical terms, a foreign investor is not barred from registering this activity in Bali today on the basis of that moratorium; the national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling remains the relevant ownership figure in this record.
